apps.name: disk
apps.title: Disk Monitor
apps.description: Disk inspection on the Windows endpoint: per-volume usage (free/used/percent), per-process write-byte I/O counters (who's writing to disk), and which process holds a given file open (Restart Manager). Environment-agnostic: the OS-bound ctypes work lives in cap:desktop.diskmon (endpoint daemon); the app degrades cleanly to 'unavailable' with no endpoint. All read_only — this app never writes. (The v1 real-time ETW file-write tracer needs elevation and is not surfaced.)

apps.name: drive_manager
apps.title: Drive Manager
apps.description: Native AppUI workspace for the owner’s Google Drive: file browser, folder tree, indexed galleries and documents, search, upload, organizing and share administration. The existing Drive service retains OAuth, data and write authorization; bounded assistant writes require explicit confirmation.

apps.name: drive_share
apps.title: Drive Share
apps.description: Public, read-only sharing of DriveManager folders: visitors with a share link browse the shared folder, view photos (gallery, map), download when allowed, and upload when the share permits it. Everything a visitor does goes through DriveManager's loopback-only internal share API, which checks the token, password, expiry, selected files and ancestry; this app holds no Google credentials. Shares are created in DriveManager. Moved from the pylon-server DriveShare service.

apps.name: gdrive
apps.title: Google Drive
apps.description: Google Drive file operations via the Drive API v3 (OAuth2 installed-app or service account). List/search/download files, and (confirm-gated) upload/mkdir/delete. OAuth client-secrets are sourced from the platform/credential vault (credential name 'gdrive-oauth-client', overridable via config.credential_name) — store them once with credential.set instead of hand-editing config.json; a config.json credentials_path still works as a fallback. The Google client libraries are optional — status reports actionable setup guidance when they or credentials aren't configured, rather than crashing. Token cache under repo data/.

apps.name: vfs
apps.title: VFS (Virtual File System)
apps.description: Location-transparent file access across backends via one self-describing URL: vfs://{endpoint}/{path}. endpoint carries its transport — file:///… or the self host (reach 'fs', this machine's real disk, in-process) or ssh://host (reach 'ssh', remote SFTP via the platform/auth_ssh app). One uniform op contract (list/tree/read/write/stat/mkdir/delete/rename) regardless of where the bytes live. Portable: no win32, no paramiko in this app — the SSH half is delegated app-to-app to platform/auth_ssh; the local half is stdlib os. Ported (minimal core) from remote_ws's VFS.

apps.name: kb_core
apps.title: Personal KB Core
apps.description: Core Personal Knowledge Base service: atomic UTF-8 bundle storage, personal annotations and collections, rebuildable SQLite FTS5 search, health audits, previewed reconciliation, AppUI viewer, and VIS provider.

apps.name: vis
apps.title: VIS — Virtual Information System
apps.description: The VIS layer: navigate HIERARCHICAL information (the tool catalog, MOM, a doc set, a code repo) one level at a time. An LLM can't read a large tree at once, so VIS lets it open a node, read its children's descriptions, and choose where to go next — multi-turn, progressive retrieval at a flat token cost per turn. Providers declare a `vis_provider` manifest block (children/node/search primitives), the framework aggregates them, and this app implements the navigation operators (open/expand/search/ancestors/…) + multi-turn session operators (focus/collapse/view) once, identical across providers. Addresses are vis://<provider>/<path>. Read-only by contract.

workspace.comment: VIS #41: knowledge/vis is the MANAGER of the VIS layer — it aggregates every provider's primitives and owns the navigation operators the workspace/sidebar use.

apps.name: book
apps.title: Book & Ebook Catalog
apps.description: Book and ebook catalog with ISBN/ASIN identity, edition-verified Amazon HTML parsing, and reading notes.

apps.name: fish
apps.title: Fish Market
apps.description: Compare seafood portions, prices and reviews from saved market research.

apps.name: gkeep
apps.title: Google Keep
apps.description: Collect the signed-in user's Google Keep notes and expose them as a searchable store + a VIS provider (notes grouped by label). Google Keep has no official API, so auth is Google's cookie-based SAPISIDHASH scheme: cookies are captured from the signed-in managed Edge via cap:system.browser.cookie (this app never drives the browser itself), then notes are fetched over plain HTTP from the private notes endpoint and stored in the app's own PylonDB realm (data/apps/personal/gkeep/keep.pylondb). Notes become browsable at vis://gkeep/<label>/<note> and their text is available for LLM/RAG. Reads are read_only; refresh/evict are confirm-gated writes into the realm.

workspace.comment: VIS_PROVIDERS_TODO #6-#10: gkeep exposes its notes (grouped by label) to the workspace as the VIS provider 'gkeep'.

apps.name: googlevm
apps.title: Google VM
apps.description: Manage Google Compute Engine instances through the official API.

apps.name: googlevm_mcp
apps.title: pylon_mcp
apps.description: Deploy and manage the authenticated MCP endpoint on Google VM: service controls, logs, OAuth connection details and VM tools.

apps.name: map
apps.title: Saved Places & Map
apps.description: Personal saved places, visited photo-location histories, reusable coordinate/address/place cache, and offline Haversine nearby search.

apps.name: movie
apps.title: Movie & AVDBS Catalog
apps.description: Movie and AVDBS metadata catalog with TMDB identity matching, conflict detection, and guarded rename plans.

apps.name: music_catalog
apps.title: Music & Classical Catalog
apps.description: Music and Classical album metadata catalog with unambiguous intake matching and links to personal/music_player.

apps.name: music_player
apps.title: Music Player
apps.description: Browse and play your Google Drive music library through VFS, with a folder tree and playback queue.

apps.name: photo
apps.title: Photo Archive
apps.description: Personal photo archive with SHA-256 deduplication, EXIF/GPS extraction, thumbnails, logical folders, incoming intake planning, and private media streaming.

apps.name: shopping
apps.title: Shopping Archive
apps.description: Saved shopping products, Coupang option identities, structured JSON-LD parsing, and price observation history.

apps.name: travel_video
apps.title: Travel Video Studio
apps.description: Data-driven travel video storyboard projects, privacy-safe GPX track analysis (stays, speed candidates, endpoint trimming), and TTS/scene timeline builder.

apps.name: web-naverblog
apps.title: Naver Blog
apps.description: Save public Naver Blog posts with ordered article text, local images and public comments; browse and search through VIS.

apps.name: web-navermap
apps.title: Naver Places
apps.description: Naver map library: collections, discovery, full review capture and analysis, photos, visits, related blogs, multi-provider directions and route exports.

apps.name: web-youtube
apps.title: YouTube Library
apps.description: Capture YouTube information on Google VM and expose fetched local copies through VIS.

apps.name: web_archive
apps.title: Web Archive & Keep Queue
apps.description: Capture and normalize web pages, FMKorea posts, and Naver Blog articles into Personal KB Core, manage the Google Keep ingestion seed queue, and detect duplicate web captures.

apps.name: youtube
apps.title: YouTube Archive
apps.description: YouTube video metadata archive with regression-guarded dynamic comment and caption track merging.

apps.name: accounts
apps.title: Accounts
apps.description: Manage owner password and linked Google / GitLab identities. Authentication stays in the gateway.

apps.name: app_manager
apps.title: App Manager
apps.description: Manage per-server app lists, external pylon-apps-* packs (e.g. Google Drive), and scaffold new apps.

apps.name: app_scenarios
apps.title: App Scenarios
apps.description: Manage and run app SCENARIOS — each is a prompt tied to the op it resolves to, its args, and an expected-output assertion, stored in each app's manifest.json `scenarios` block (doubling as example prompts AND live acceptance tests). Two run modes per scenario: 'direct' (call the op and assert on its output) and 'llm' (drive the natural-language prompt through ai/llm_server with tools — a TRUE end-to-end test of the user path, where the model discovers + calls the tools itself, with vfs/tool support). list/add/remove scenarios and run them against the running framework. Write-op scenarios are authored preview-only so a run never fires a real mutation.

apps.name: appui_guide
apps.title: AppUI Guide
apps.description: The 'how to build an app' hub: a live gallery that demonstrates each AppUI component (with runnable demos + the exact code + which bundle ships it), a one-click new-app scaffolder (wraps tools/new_app.py + hot-adds via /v1/admin/discover), and the framework docs surfaced in-page (AGENTS.md, the AppUI README, PANEL_CONTRACT.md).

apps.name: auth_ftp
apps.title: Auth FTP (connection app)
apps.description: The FTP CONNECTION app — owns all FTP connection logic: anonymous (and future credential-injected) GET/stream/listing over ftp://. Apps hold NO FTP transport; they call auth_ftp (directly, or via platform/downloader's `ftp` source plugin, which routes through this app the way the http/cpistore plugins route through auth_http). Anonymous public FTP (e.g. ftp.3gpp.org) works today; the per-host credential seam reads any secret from platform/credential (never stored/logged here). Pure stdlib (urllib) — no win32, no browser. Symmetric partner of platform/auth_http and platform/auth_ssh.

apps.name: auth_http
apps.title: Auth HTTP (connection app)
apps.description: The HTTP CONNECTION app — owns all HTTP connection logic: credential-injected fetch/write, browser-bound (MSAL/cookie) token acquisition, per-product auth-header + token-lifecycle PLUGINS, 401->refresh->retry, and live test/status. Apps hold NO connection logic; they call auth_http. The secret itself lives in platform/credential (the sealed vault): auth_http reads the raw secret in_process (token/master_get), builds the request with its own plugins, and persists a rotated token back via credential.put_rotated. Symmetric partner of platform/auth_ssh.

apps.name: auth_ssh
apps.title: Connection (SSH/SFTP)
apps.description: Portable SSH/SFTP sessions + remote exec, lifted from remote_ws. Holds per-(user,host) in-RAM SSH credentials (password / private-key / agent) with idle TTL; keeps a persistent SSHClient per host (DNS TTL cache, preflight socket reuse, liveness probe, transient-only retry-with-backoff) and a DEDICATED SFTP transport with a per-connection channel queue (paramiko SFTPClient is not thread-safe). Pure paramiko + stdlib — no win32, no CDP. SSH credentials live only in process memory, never logged, never returned.

apps.name: code_sync
apps.title: Code Sync
apps.description: Coordinate GitHub version history and Google Drive editable source exchange; stage incoming changes without changing active code.

apps.name: credential
apps.title: Credential Store
apps.description: The SEALED SECRET VAULT. Stores credentials/accounts (Fernet-sealed by default via a machine-derived key; seals via cap:system.secrets.dpapi when an endpoint provides it) and the shared master account. Vault-only: descriptor CRUD (list/set/delete), in_process raw-secret reads (token/master_get) and a narrow rotation write-back (put_rotated). ALL HTTP connection logic — fetch/refresh/test/status/browser-token minting + the per-product plugins — now lives in platform/auth_http; only auth_http/auth_ssh touch this vault. Secrets never persist in code, pages, logs, or responses (redacted on read); the store lives under data/, gitignored.

apps.name: daemon_manager
apps.title: Daemon Manager
apps.description: Inspect execution endpoints and manage owner-approved device enrollment, heartbeat, capabilities, capacity and redacted jobs.

apps.name: deploy
apps.title: Deploy
apps.description: Brings pylon-server up on an endpoint. AppForge: a signed snapshot of only the aiweb foundation (main.py, pyproject.toml, framework/aiweb) is pushed to GitLab, AppForge builds and deploys it, then the framework, browser dependencies and apps are uploaded over HTTP and hot-plugged. Google VM: personal/googlevm starts the VM, the foundation is installed over SSH as a user service, then the same upload; the Linux daemon can take over as the bootstrap. Local (Windows): the daemon at login. The apps sent are the committed ones plus those the launchpad's deployment rules allow for the target.

apps.name: downloader
apps.title: Downloader
apps.description: Fetch a document from an internal SOURCE (Eridoc, MediaWiki, …) by URL and return its bytes + resolved filename + metadata. Each source is a PLUGIN (framework.plugins) that claims URLs by pattern and fetches with auth borrowed app-to-app from the platform/credential app. Portable: no win32; stdlib HTTP + the credential app. New sources are drop-in plugin modules — the app and its ops never change.

apps.name: feedback
apps.title: Feedback
apps.description: A standalone Feedback app that files bugs / ideas into the issue_report fleet tracker. It is the page-or-sidebar embodiment of the shared AppUIFeedback component (the same one the workspace app embeds as a tab): ONE mount() renders either as a full page OR as a sidebar panel, via AppUIPanelApp — the reusable 'page ⇄ sidebar' duality pattern. No new backend; it submits to the issue_report app.

apps.name: googleauth
apps.title: Google Auth
apps.description: Google API connection and OAuth setup; separate from Pylon owner login.

apps.name: home
apps.title: Home
apps.description: The pylon-server launchpad served at /: a live, VIS-driven home that browses every app and LLM tool (vis://tool_catalog groups → apps → tools, plus any other VIS provider such as the Ericsson MOM), with search, a command palette, pinned/recent apps, a fleet pulse, endpoint status, a right-click app tree, and a Try-it runner for read-only tools. Also the pylon-server project registry and handoff (projects page: TODO, services, checkpoints, resume briefs, the operations view and VM-only private-GitHub sync), merged from ProjectHub.

apps.name: issue_report
apps.title: Issue Report
apps.description: Issue / defect tracker: user feedback and converter rendering gaps (the 'submit' backend platform/feedback depends on) AND recurring ERRORS FROM THE LOG - one issue per log fingerprint with an ISS-n number, occurrences, first/last seen, an automatic triage class + reason, a comment thread, and the number written back onto the log entries as a comment. A resolved issue whose error keeps happening is re-opened as a regression. Store: data/apps/platform/issue_report/. Read ops are read_only; writes are confirm (delete and the bulk track_log self-gate on confirm=true).

apps.name: log
apps.title: Logs
apps.description: Unified structured application, framework, browser and endpoint logs.

apps.name: mcp_server
apps.title: MCP Bridge
apps.description: Model Context Protocol server — the OUTWARD bridge that exposes every platform tool to EXTERNAL MCP clients (Claude Desktop, other agents) over standards-compliant JSON-RPC (initialize/tools/list/tools/call/ping). Unlike platform/tool_catalog (the internal anti-MCP browse surface), this speaks real MCP. tools/list is enumerated LIVE from platform/tool_catalog so a new app's tools appear automatically; tools/call routes to apphost.invoke(require_facet='tool'). Served as an op (rpc) AND as a Streamable-HTTP mount at /apps/platform/mcp_server/mcp. WRITE (safety=confirm) tools require confirm=true in the call arguments unless MCP_ALLOW_WRITES=1.

apps.name: ops
apps.title: Operations
apps.description: Operations for this pylon-server host: a dependency-ordered task executor (install, services, health, regression tests, monitor, backup/restore, deploy prerequisites, scaffold, security audit, and acceptance gates that need recorded end-to-end evidence), host metrics, verified backups of the runtime databases and a secret-file audit. VM-only checks (systemd, deploy) report 'skipped' elsewhere. Moved from the pylon-server Todo project.

apps.name: os_page_input
apps.title: OS Page Input
apps.description: Drive a TOP-FRAME web page with real OS-level input — a genuine OS mouse-click to focus an element, then genuine OS keystrokes — the way a human types, so a page cannot distinguish it from a user. Complements platform/page_automation (which drives the managed browser via CDP) for fields/frameworks that ignore synthetic DOM/CDP input. The FIRST consumer of framework.os_automation: it reads the target element's rect + window dims over CDP (the browser must already expose a debug port), computes the absolute screen click point with the verified viewport-to-screen math, then OS-clicks + OS-types via cap:desktop.input and reads the value back to confirm it landed. Environment-agnostic: all OS side effects live in cap:desktop.input on the endpoint. Constraints: top-frame elements only (cannot reach a cross-origin OOPIF), and needs an interactive desktop session. type_into is confirm-gated (a real OS side effect) and self-gates on confirm=true with a dry-run plan preview.

apps.name: page_automation
apps.title: Page Automation (login cases)
apps.description: The single source of truth for BROWSER page-automation CASES — named recipes (match + screen classification rules + selectors + actions) that drive a login/consent flow in the managed Edge via cap:system.cdp. Replaces the hardcoded screen state machines that lived inline in the daemon device_login and in workspace/cdp_session. Cases are editable DATA under data/apps/platform/page_automation/cases/ (hot-add a flow with no code change). This app is environment-agnostic: it stores/serves/matches cases and resolves a case BUNDLE for the daemon interpreter; the daemon device_login cap consumes the bundle and does the actual CDP driving. Secrets are never stored or echoed here — a case references a secret by ref (e.g. 'master'); the orchestrator (auth_http) resolves it from platform/credential in-process.

apps.name: remote_runner
apps.title: Remote Runner
apps.description: Remote command / file-copy / OS-tag detection + DETACHED durable jobs on configured hosts, layered on platform/auth_ssh (one SSH stack, one credential path, one host-alias registry — no parallel ssh). run adds the SELI 'module add' prelude + a done/connect phase; os_tag maps uname→RHEL8-x86_64 for per-OS build trees; copy uploads/downloads a file over SFTP. Detached jobs (job_launch/status/log/cancel/list) run a setsid process that SURVIVES the ssh channel, recording pid/log/rc/status under a per-user job root — the durable-job fabric seqdiag_harvester / cask_manager need. Ported from ai-pylon v1 remote_runner, step 1 of 2 (step 2 adds the port-forwarding fabric: tcp_pipe / run_pushing / persistent -L tunnel).

apps.name: router
apps.title: Router
apps.description: The public hostnames of this host: the Caddy routes it owns (the VM's DriveManager, DriveShare, pylon-server and pylon-server hosts, the ProjectHub path and the hub redirect), reconciled through Caddy's localhost admin API with every other route preserved, plus read-only diagnostics and the versioned root Caddyfile. Hosts without Caddy (Windows, AppForge) report that routing is done elsewhere. Moved from the pylon-server Router project.

apps.name: settings
apps.title: Settings & Home
apps.description: Instance HOME + global settings. Shows a launcher of every loaded app (page link + example prompts, built live from the app registry) and lets you view/edit the global workspace root + default workspace (framework.settings, stored under ~/pylon-server/) plus see the legacy-config migration. The workspace app is the center of pylon-server; this is the front door + the one place the shared workspace_root is configured.

apps.name: tool_cask
apps.title: Tool Cask
apps.description: The CASK marketplace (skills + agents) as a platform tool source: search, install into a host's .kiro, uninstall, submit/publish a skill folder, download + browse artifacts, and a VIS tree (vis://cask). Every cask command runs with the cask CLI ON the SSH host (platform/auth_ssh) where the Cloudflare Access session lives. Also: login (one-click, or fully automatic via the managed Edge), an unattended CASK_API_KEY, publish of the sysdoc-converter bundle, and sync. Formerly ericsson/cask_manager; absorbed the Workspace's mcp_cask.

apps.name: tool_catalog
apps.title: Tool Catalog
apps.description: A HIERARCHICAL, browsable catalog of every tool the platform exposes — built from the apps' declared `tool` facets (manifest), grouped by their app-group path (system/, office/outlook/, …). This is the deliberate alternative to a flat MCP tool dump: an AI chat (or a human) BROWSES into the catalog (group → tools → detail) and pulls only the few schemas it needs, so tool discovery stays context-cheap at any scale. Its ops are pure discovery and never execute a tool; its PAGE (Tools / Chain builder / Dependency graph / API reference) calls tools through the normal op edge - Try-It and the chain builder, whose steps route earlier outputs into later inputs. Keyword recommend + capability-gap capture today; an LLM-ranked recommend is wired once the llm app exists.

workspace.comment: VIS #41: the tool catalog is the reference VIS provider 'tool_catalog' (groups -> apps -> tools via vis_children/vis_node/vis_search).

apps.name: tool_guides
apps.title: Tool Guides
apps.description: Hierarchical guides for using apps and tools correctly (root > group > app > tool, + cross-app recipes): each guide says when to use it, lists its tools, worked scenarios and notes. Also learns each assistant's favourite tools from its successful use and a tool relationship map; ai/llm_server puts the guide index + favourites into every assistant's prompt.

workspace.comment: platform plumbing for the AI assistants; its guide tree is also the VIS provider 'tool_guides'.

apps.name: tool_kiro
apps.title: Tool Kiro
apps.description: Recognises the .kiro folders - home (~/.kiro), this repo, the active workspace folder and any extra or remote root (file/vfs) - and puts what they declare to work across the platform: MCP servers (settings/mcp.json, agents' mcpServers) become catalog tools mcp/<server>.<tool> once enabled, usable by assistants, the chain builder, Try-It and workflows; skills (skills/*/SKILL.md) become guides in platform/tool_guides; agents (agents/*.json) become chat personas (prompt + resources + tool scope); steering is listed. Browsable as vis://kiro. Nothing is contacted until a server is enabled. Also the platform's MCP registries (the Ericsson bnew allowlist): its servers are enabled the same way (stdio ones run on the configured SSH host), with per-server env values.

workspace.comment: exposes the user's .kiro (MCP/skills/agents/steering) to the workspace, its chat and every assistant

apps.name: tool_profiler
apps.title: Tool Profiler
apps.description: Per-tool call metrics (calls, errors, avg/p50/p95/max latency), recent traces, slow calls and usage analytics for EVERY tool call on the host - recorded by the framework itself (framework.op_metrics, fed by apphost.invoke), so HTTP, in-process, LLM tool calls and workflow steps are all counted. In memory since the host started; parameter values are never recorded. The v2 port of v1 tools_profiler + Tool Analytics.

apps.name: tool_runner
apps.title: Tool Runner
apps.description: Workflows over app tools - the v2 port of v1 tools_runner: a flow engine (tool / condition / switch / loop / parallel / transform / sub-workflow / map-reduce / approval / agent / llm / http steps), the visual workflow editor, cron + event + file-watch + webhook triggers, run history with replay, step replay and retry-from-step, agents and pipelines, the offline queue, a planner and Power Automate import. Tool metrics live in platform/tool_profiler; Try-It and the API reference in platform/tool_catalog.

apps.name: tool_todo
apps.title: TODO
apps.description: The TODO list of every app (framework apps, pylon-server projects and the bootstrap): one TODO.md per app folder in the pylon-server todo format (persistent #N ids, sections, notes, dated done trail). List one app or the counts of all; add, complete, annotate and set the state of items.

apps.name: work_runner
apps.title: Work Runner
apps.description: General background job queue: submit-and-poll long-running work instead of blocking a request. A bounded drain loop (max 2 concurrent) runs each job to a terminal state and persists queue + history under data/apps/platform/work_runner/. Jobs target local (subprocess) or remote (via platform/remote_runner), kind run|copy, with optional inline-script / VFS env-file staging (file/vfs). Progress/terminal state is posted to system/notify. Ported from ai-pylon v1 (SELI/cask composite job kinds deferred). Read ops are read_only; submit/cancel are safety=confirm.

apps.name: cdp
apps.title: CDP Inspector
apps.description: Inspect and drive the endpoint's signed-in browser via the CDP capability: list tabs, navigate, and evaluate JavaScript. Environment-agnostic — calls cap('cap:system.cdp'); the actual Edge/DevTools lives in the endpoint daemon.

apps.name: clipboard
apps.title: Clipboard
apps.description: Read the system clipboard (text / files / HTML / image) and the source app, with a local bounded HISTORY (capture/history/search/pin). Environment-agnostic app fronting cap:desktop.clipboard (the pure-ctypes capture core lives in the Windows endpoint daemon). A scheduler polls `sequence` and calls `capture` to build history; pattern triggers + a clipboard.copied event are the remaining daemon-side follow-up.

apps.name: node_sync
apps.title: Node Sync (HTTP)
apps.description: HTTP-based peer-to-peer code and data synchronization between Pylon nodes (local <-> VM) with SHA-256 diff, selective push/pull, secret exclusion, and automatic pre-overwrite backups. Requires no SSH client.

apps.name: notify
apps.title: Notification Hub
apps.description: Persistent notification center and delivery hub. Desktop tray status, lifecycle and menus are owned by system/tray; legacy tray_* operations delegate there.

apps.name: remote_browser
apps.title: Remote Browser
apps.description: Human-operated remote Chromium workspace with an endpoint selector, isolated profiles and an embedded browser viewer.

apps.name: resources
apps.title: Resources
apps.description: Report + free the real idle resource consumers of the platform. v2 apps are in-process (free at idle), so the things that actually spin RAM/CPU when idle live in the endpoint daemon: the managed Edge browser, the kiro ACP warm pool, and keep-awake. This app reports them and releases them on demand (the v2 answer to v1's 'stop idle apps'). Environment-agnostic â€” drives cap:system.cdp / cap:system.acp / cap:desktop.wakeup.

apps.name: server_conn
apps.title: Server Connectivity
apps.description: Inspect accessible IPs and URLs for the current Pylon HTTP server, and configure server binding, DuckDNS dynamic DNS, and daemon-managed ngrok tunnels.

apps.name: ssh_client
apps.title: SSH Client
apps.description: Manage SSH keys, ~/.ssh/config host entries, GCE instance SSH key provisioning, connection checks, and remote command execution for standard SSH clients.

apps.name: task_analyzer
apps.title: Task Analyzer
apps.description: Task manager / analyzer: live process table, top CPU/memory consumers, per-process detail, the process parent->child tree, a one-shot 'what's using the machine right now' analysis (summary + top consumers + per-program rollup + verdict), and a guarded process kill. Core is a pure psutil wrapper with a fast Windows PDH backend (per-process CPU+memory in one query, ~15x faster) that falls back to psutil automatically. Read ops are read_only; kill is safety=confirm and refuses critical OS/session processes unless force_protected=true. Ported from ai-pylon v1.

apps.name: terminal
apps.title: Terminal
apps.description: Run commands on the endpoint machine OR on a remote host over SSH. LOCAL shells broker cap:system.terminal (real ConPTY on the Windows daemon). REMOTE shells (host set) route through platform/auth_ssh (portable paramiko SSH) with credentials from platform/credential — no daemon needed. `run` is the clean one-shot path with a REAL exit code and split stdout/stderr, local or remote. Local also offers persistent interactive PTY sessions (create/write/read/exec/resize/kill). The xterm page (xterm.htm, mounted API /apps/system/terminal/xterm/) is a real terminal emulator: SSH to any host with host-key confirmation (passwords used once, never stored), or a local shell (PTY on Linux, the daemon's ConPTY on Windows; off on ai-web pods).

apps.name: tray
apps.title: System Tray
apps.description: Manage desktop tray status, lifecycle, and application menus.

apps.name: ui_input
apps.title: Input Simulation
apps.description: OS-level keyboard/mouse input simulation — injects genuine physical input events (so a browser/app receives real OS input). Environment-agnostic front for cap:desktop.input; the pynput core lives in the Windows endpoint daemon. Write ops (type/key/mouse) are confirm-gated (real OS side effect).

apps.name: wakeup
apps.title: Keep Awake
apps.description: Prevent the machine (and display) from sleeping, with physical-idle backoff. Environment-agnostic app fronting cap:desktop.wakeup (the ctypes keep-awake core lives in the Windows endpoint daemon).
